utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We have a few procedural items still pending. I leave it a bit to the parties whether we start with them or that we do it later this afternoon. But I see that the Prosecution is there with a strong team, so it might be that they would like to express themselves on some of the issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. You're quite correct. Mr. Gaynor is here for the purpose of addressing one of those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of those issues, and that would be which one, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It concerns the request for videoconference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to conflicting treaty obligations, safe conduct, et cetera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, let me first of all ask you whether the Defence has already filed a response to that motion, because I haven't seen it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's on its way right now, Your Honour. I signed it about 25 minutes ago and it's on its way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be of any use to first read that response and then postpone it to later this afternoon? Perhaps the Chamber during the break could also look at a response. Because I take it, Mr. Stewart, since the issue of the conflicting treaty obligations has been raised last Friday that we find something in your response as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, you don't, Your Honour, on that. We haven't gone into that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then if not, then I would not --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I can explain why, because we weren't just being difficult. After all, the issue having been raised in court the other day it did really seem to us that it was primarily for the Prosecution then to make further investigations on that question to support their motion. So obviously we will look at anything at the appropriate time, but that did seem a fair order and avoid unnecessary work and duplication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, how much time would you need to address this specific issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very little time, Your Honour, I can tell you right now in about two sentences. We have reconsidered the position in the light of Your Honours' interpretations of the Headquarter agreement and in light of the general preference for in-court testimony as opposed to videoconference testimony. For those reasons we have decided not to pursue our request for videolink testimony. And in all other respects, the motion remains the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's a clear answer. Of course, our interpretation is very important, but of course most important for safe conducts is the interpretation by the Dutch government of the host agreement, isn't it, because they have to refrain from whatever one might have in mind. Then we'll look at the matter, but first read the response by the Defence. Any other issue, procedural issue, to be raised urgently?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a practical issue as opposed to strictly a procedural issue, which is this: I was informed yesterday by Ms. Cmeric that there had been a problem about the installation of the appropriate software in Mr. Krajisnik's computer at the UN Detention Unit, so as to enable him to listen to B/C/S audiotapes of previous evidence in other cases, transcripts from other cases. Not surprisingly, Your Honour, I tend to leave nuts and bolts like that to other members of the team. I didn't realise until yesterday that this was a continuing problem. Neither did Ms. Cmeric. It had been reported to her. But the current position is that Mr. Krajisnik does not have this facility and is therefore unable -- he can listen to audiotapes where they're available of interviews, because it's a different software, I understand, without my being able to go into that, but he can't listen to transcripts of previous evidence. That's clearly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are stored on what medium? CD-ROMs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not normal audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I said a audiotapes. I was using that in a rather loose generic way, I think, Your Honour. Because I believe that they are on CD-ROMs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what confused me slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. I beg your pardon, Your Honour. The programme is called an FTR programme, apparently, but again, don't ask me to go any further on that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that already a start was made this morning to resolve that problem and that the Detention Unit and all the technicians have to work together one way or the other, but they are quite busy in establishing such a working relationship at this moment. So with this information, I think I stay out, the Chamber stays out for a little while and see whether it is resolved. If not, then we'll further pursue the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm grateful, Your Honour. I was actually going to say exactly the same, that I certainly intend to stay out of it as much as possible. But I'm grateful for the Trial Chamber's support when needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any other procedural issue? I've got a few on my list, but I'm not insisting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, nothing that needs to be addressed immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then may I just mention a few matters that first of all I received an e-mail, copy of an e-mail, which confirms that the investigators, Defence investigators, could come on the 4th and 5th of November. I don't know whether the parties have already discussed what consequences it this would have for the court schedule of that week, especially in view of witnesses to be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have discussed that and we've tried to adjust our calendar accordingly. We were going to try to move up one of the witnesses scheduled for next week to this week but he had a passport problem so we weren't able to do that. So our plan is to have two witnesses for those three days and one of the three witnesses that was scheduled to begin on Monday will be moved to the following Monday, November 8th. I can provide an updated schedule to the Defence counsel and the Court later on today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So that has the attention of the parties. Then your comments on what I would call the court schedule, long-term court schedule, perhaps we wait, but are the parties ready to comment on it, as I indicated last Friday, I think, that both parties would have ten minutes and then, if needed another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Generally speaking, we are ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the Defence be ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Actually, I'm not really ready today, Your Honour. I didn't appreciate we were going to be asked today. We can make ourselves ready of course fairly quickly, but not today, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll leave it for today and I'll come back to it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then is the Defence -- is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher. And I take it that this is Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is Mr. Radic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, yes, Predrag Radic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, do you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Radic. Mr. Radic, you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I begin, I would note that when Mr. Radic testified previously in the Brdjanin case he did receive a caution pursuant to Rule 90. I don't know if the Court wanted to renew that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, the counsel for the Prosecution, Mr. Tieger, has asked me to draw your attention to Rule 90 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Did you have any specific -- you mean the 90(E) caution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had no intention of trumping the Court's intentions, but I didn't know if you had an opportunity to be aware of the procedure that was followed in Brdjanin. Obviously, the witness is aware of what happened in that case, and if the Court feels that no further attention is necessary I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not been informed about -- is the caution about the right of an accused to oppose against answering a question? That's what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. I think Judge Agius referred to him as a protagonist in the events and therefore out of an abundance of caution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, as I'm just told was done in -- during your testimony in the Brdjanin case, I draw your attention to Rule 90(E), which reads that: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate himself." If you would object to answering any question that might incriminate yourself, this Chamber, however, can compel you to answer the question, but if you are compelled in this way, your answer cannot be used as evidence in a subsequent proceedings against yourself. Apart from that, you're still under a duty to speak the truth, and therefore, if -- the only possible prosecution if this Rule will be applied is that if you would make a false statement, which of course this Chamber does not expect you to do. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Radic. We've not met --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- before. I'm Alan Tieger, I'm with the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'll be asking you questions first and then the Defence will have an opportunity to ask questions, as will the Court.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can begin by familiarising the Court a bit with your background. You currently live in Banja Luka and are a Serb by ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you still a professor on the economic faculty at Banja Luka University; sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And are you still involved as a director of the local brewery?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you are the president currently of a small political party known as the Democratic Patriotic Party?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could turn your attention to the multi-party elections in 1990. Were you asked at that time by the SDS to consent to have your name put forward by them as a candidate for office?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in November of 1990, were you elected president of the Municipal Assembly for Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did you assume that office in January of 1991?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that after your election, you then in fact joined the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: After that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And a couple of more preliminary matters. In July of 1991, were you elected to the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in 1992, did you become a member of the ARK Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff for the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: By virtue of my position as president in the municipality, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic, during the course of your activities, political activities, in 1990 and thereafter, did you have an opportunity to meet and work with various members of the SDS and Bosnian Serb leadership?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Through the Main Board, basically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You attended meetings of the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And those were meetings at which SDS policy was formulated?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also attend various gatherings or assemblies at which the municipal, regional, and republic leaders of the SDS, and later the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, gathered?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I don't know which gatherings you mean. If you mean meetings where opinions were expressed, then the answer is yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me give you an example of one such meeting and direct your attention to a meeting that was held on February 14th, 1992, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TEIGER
utterances.text: And in that connection, Your Honour, I would draw the Court's attention to Prosecution's Exhibit 67A, tab 27. That's the binder of intercepts and speeches adduced during the course of Mr. Treanor's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic, this is indicated as an extended session of the Main and Executive Board of the SDS, held in the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo. And by way of directing your attention to some of what was discussed at that meeting and to your own presence there, perhaps I'll be able to bring your attention to one particular part of that meeting. Now, Mr. Radic, to assist you in identifying the location in the B/C/S, I would note that working backwards in the text, you will see one cut -- indication of a cut in the recording, and then a second one. And it's at that second spot that I wish to draw your attention briefly. That's on page 24, Your Honours, of the 31-page English translation. This is Dr. Karadzic speaking and Dr. Karadzic states, beginning at line 15 [sic] of page 24: "And, as regards the essence, of which Mr. Radic spoke, now, please, that is why we called you today, to intensify, to introduce the 'second level'" -- second level is in quotes -- "and to intensify the functioning of the government at any cost and on every single millimetre of our territory. Now I'm asking you for a break, what do you say, half an hour?" Mr. Radic, is the meeting of February 14th, 1992 in Sarajevo an example of the kind of meetings you spoke of when you talked about your attendance at gatherings, meetings at which opinions were expressed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, you know how it is. This is a very long document for me to be able to say. But yes, I do remember that meeting and I arrived at the meeting feeling very ill. And after the break, I in fact left the meeting. And I wasn't able to say anything afterwards, later on. But as far as I am able to gather from what I have here, it was a question of forming the executive organs which in actual fact didn't exist. So this was the beginnings. The 28th of February, 1992 we were still not at war and we didn't have any state organs, no state organs of any kind, on the 28th of February, in actual fact. So in the municipalities, this led us into a position in which we tried to find solutions for everything that we weren't able to do and receive from the state, coming down to us, the executive organs or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I appreciate your effort to comment on the text, but my question for the moment was limited to the more simple question of your recollection of your attendance at that meeting. Perhaps a little later in the proceeding I'll be able to present you with a copy of your own remarks on that occasion. Now, in addition to your attendance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just a bit confused about the witness talking about the 28th of February. Could you clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Court correctly brings our attention to the fact that you mentioned the 28th of February in your answer. I believe that you were referring to this particular document, which is dated the 14th, and so I just want to clarify whether this was just a mistaken recollection of the date or you were referring to something else.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: No. Quite simply, this document, this material that you have just given me, I'm seeing for the first time in this shape and form. All right. It's the 14th of February, as it says here. So it is even clearer, then, that we didn't have any organs and that this was a meeting, as far as I can see - I would have to read through it all to remember all the details - but anyway, it was a meeting devoted to the formation of organs that we were lacking at that time, that we didn't have in Republika Srpska. Nor did Republika Srpska itself exist at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I just wanted to clarify the date, and I appreciate that clarification. Now, in addition to attending meetings of the Main Board, your attendance at meetings such as the gathering on February 14th, 1992, did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you also participate with leaders of the SDS and Republika Srpska at rallies?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: There were a certain number of rallies. One such rally was presented to me in the Brdjanin trial. However, I did not say what I said there, but I did take part in meetings, in rallies. It was a way in which we could express our views about what was going on on the soil of the former Yugoslavia. So if I can put it this way, it was the dissolution of Yugoslavia. And without asking a constituent peoples. So a rally was a way in which we could say that we didn't agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, may I ask your attention for the following: You were asked whether you participated with leaders of the SDS and the Republika Srpska at rallies. You gave a lot of details on what you expect the rally to be, on which questions that will follow focussing, but we do not know that yet. The question was quite simple: Whether you participated in such rallies. In the next questions Mr. Tieger will ask you for further details. We are under some time constraints. Could I ask you to listen carefully to the question and first of all answer that question, and then wait for another question. If there would be something important finally missing, you always can address the Chamber and say: Well, I'd like to add a few things on the questions already put to me. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like marked as next in order a video, which is B/C/S V000-4757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P354, and the transcript, P354A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you referred to a video of a rally that you were shown during the Brdjanin case. I'd like to quickly play a couple of excerpts from that tape for the benefit of this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is important for the transcript, Mr. Tieger, that whatever is said in B/C/S will be translated in English, because otherwise it doesn't appear in the French transcript either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could play clip 1 of video 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The meeting was opened by Predrag Radic, the President of the Municipal Assembly of Banja Luka, with the following message. 'Twice they slaughtered us. We were forgiven but not forgotten. If they try to do the same for the third time we shall neither forgive nor forget, regardless of how non-Christian it may be.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Radic, the video depicts you at that rally; is that right? That was the portion we just saw?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And although on the video it's possible to hear some of your words, what we heard in court today was the announcer paraphrasing what you said. Do you recall your precise words on that occasion? And did the -- do you know the -- can you tell us the extent to which the announcer captured the gist of what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember all the details in the exact words that I uttered on the occasion, in that year. The journalist did convey what, in his opinion, it was that I said. However, the message was quite clear. The message I sent out was a clear one, to this effect: that those who slaughtered us twice should not attempt to do so a third time. It would be Christian to forgive, but not to forget. We cannot forget. And it was at that point that I think the Prosecutor, said that I instilled fear into the population by saying that on that occasion. Unfortunately, gentlemen, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: That time, not only did they slaughterer us; they cut off our heads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you are telling us about what someone said at a certain moment. This Chamber is not aware of it. This Chamber does not know of that. So there's no reason to deny or to respond to that. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Radic, was that in effect a warning to those who would consider taking the steps that you were discussing?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: As I said, that was only a warning. It was not a threat. It was just a warning that they should not proceed along those lines. Because I myself am a victim of World War II, of acts of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that this was a rally just before the plebiscite of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I think that's it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that there was a view among the SDS leadership, and perhaps the Serbian people in general - you can tell us - that those who did not vote in the plebiscite and who did not show solidarity with the Serbian people were, in effect, traitors?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I really can't say that that was the general view. But it was to be expected that the Serbian people would declare themselves in a plebiscite to remain within Yugoslavia. Now, whether they called them traitors or not, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The rally itself was intended to respond -- the rally itself and the plebiscite, was intended to respond to the intentions of Muslims, at least as seen by the SDS, to have Bosnia leave Yugoslavia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, not only the SDS, I don't think, but the Serbian people in general. The Serb people were generally against stepping down from Yugoslavia, for well-known reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is it correct that subsequent to the plebiscite, that the question of who had acted in solidarity with the Serbian people, and in particular, who had or had not voted in the plebiscite, was used as a measure to determine certain actions against those people, such as dismissals from positions?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: How could you know how people voted at a plebiscite? It's an assumption that that could be used as a basis for one or another measure to be taken. But I should like to ask you how we could do this. We in Banja Luka could not know, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just intervene. From the answer, it appears that either the question has not been properly translated or not been fully understood by the witness. Mr. Tieger, you asked about who had or had not voted, whereas it seems that the witness has understood this as how people had voted rather than whether they had voted. So the question was whether - at least that's how it appears in English - that not how people had voted, but whether or not they had voted was used as a measure to determine certain actions against those people, such as dismissals from positions. That was the question. From your answer, I understood that you either had it wrongly translated or not fully understood. Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It couldn't have been a basis for anybody to have been dismissed from their job, and in Banja Luka, at least, not in Banja Luka where I was the president of the Municipal Assembly. Things like that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have marked next in order an article from Oslobodjenje of November 12th, 1991, entitled "You should better give yourselves up."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number --?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution number P355.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, I believe this is a document you had an opportunity to see during the course of your testimony in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this -- the article quotes Mr. Brdjanin, at that time the deputy chairman of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina, as proposing that all directors and other managers who did not take part in the plebiscite be urgently dismissed in their positions in the entire Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina. And further down the article, it quotes Mr. Brdjanin as indicating that such people should tender their resignations right away because we shall find out their names in a few days when he we check the lists of voters. Mr. Radic, regardless of your own position that it was absurd to use voting in the plebiscite as a test for retention or dismissal from positions, is it correct that Mr. Brdjanin and others took the position that such dismissals should occur?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: From this we can see that that is right. That was their position. But it didn't turn out that way. That's not what happened. And I can prove it. I can prove that things like that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, we'll get into the question of dismissals further on during the course of our question and answer. If you would wait on that, and you'll have an opportunity to address that. During the course of your testimony in Brdjanin, you also had an opportunity to see an intercepted transcript of an intercepted telephone conversation and indeed listen to an audiotape of that intercepted telephone conversation, one involving you, Mr. Brdjanin, and Mr. Vukic and Dr. Karadzic. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I do recall it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as you indicated during the course of your testimony, that was a conversation that took place after the publication of this article and after Mr. Brdjanin had taken the position that is described in the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Your Honour in that respect I'd like to have marked for identification, an intercepted telephone conversation, transcript of an intercepted telephone conversation, ERN 03083923 through 03083933.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I take it that you want to tender that as an exhibit. Marking for identification is often used for another use of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You're quite right, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, let me direct your attention to a particular portion of that intercepted telephone conversation. And that's found in the English translation toward the second half of page 4 and onward, beginning with Mr. Vukic speaking, who says: "Dr. Vukic: Well, that's great. Here's Radic for a bit.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: Put him on.

utterances.speaker: DR. VUKIC SAYS
utterances.text: I have mostly understood these options and am sticking right to them.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: DR. VUKIC SAYS
utterances.text: Therefore there's no problem as far as Brdjo and Radic and I are concerned.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: Well, fine. Brdjo was a bit out of order. I tried to get him off the hook by saying it was a joke. Fuck him. (He laughs.)

utterances.speaker: DR. VUKIC SAYS
utterances.text: Okay, he was out of order, he didn't fuck... He didn't say that. No...

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, never mind. What --

utterances.speaker: DR. VUKIC SAYS
utterances.text: ...Brdjo can't say that for his own sake or that... because Brdjo is like a guard.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No. That thing about directors, about directors and -- Vukic: Er, directors?

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: DR. VUKIC
utterances.text: Very well, then, we'll... it will have to be done, it doesn't need to be explained.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: Well, umm, well, fuck him. Instead of working and keeping quiet he doesn't work but talks.

utterances.speaker: DR. VUKIC SAYS
utterances.text: Dead right.

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: Now... he's working hard and there's no talk, fuck him. (Laughs.) And then Dr. Vukic says: Mhmm. Here's Radic for a bit. It's okay, boss. Take care." Now, in part, this telephone conversation was about the newspaper article we just looked at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And what Mr. Brdjanin was already saying in November 1991 was that people who were not considered loyal to the Serbian state should be dismissed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we looked earlier at, a few moments ago, at your comments from the rally, the plebiscite rally of November of 1991. I'd like to direct your attention and the Chamber's attention to the remarks of a couple of other participants in the rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could play clip 2, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "All dark forces for different reasons want to topple our common homeland, to divide us up. And I hope that we will not allow that to happen."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And clip 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before we go on, although it may seem obvious to you, if you could just identify that speaker, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And clip 3, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "...to tell the truth, justice and -- to tell about what's happening in the region. "On the 10th of November, by voting to stay in the joint state with all the Serbian lands and all those who wish to stay with us, we hope to once and for all put a circle by state where there will be no traitors, a state that will not fall apart every 20 years."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Radic, if you could identify those two speakers at the November 1991 rally.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: The second one was Mr. Velibor Ostojic, and the third one was quite recognisable. It was Mr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, in addition to your position as a member of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I make a suggestion which may be found helpful for the future, which is this: that if a witness is going to be asked to come along and look at a video clip of Mr. Krajisnik or Mr. Ostojic or Mr. Karadzic, then in future, we need not trouble witnesses with that sort of thing, because if the Prosecution would like to run that material past us in advance, we can actually quite reliably identify Mr. Krajisnik. That's not a difficult one for us. Mr. Karadzic is also not very difficult and I don't think Mr. Ostojic would be difficult. We will do that and we will save everybody's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Your Honour. That's very gracious of Mr. Stewart, and I appreciate it, but I don't believe the time savings will be considerable. But we'll certainly take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: They may be cumulative.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It would not have obviated the need to show the video, in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. These are short questions on whether the witness recognised the speakers. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, I began to ask you the following: In addition to your membership on the ARK Crisis Staff were you also a member of the Banja Luka municipal Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I explained it all the last time, and although Honourable Judge said that this was another case, well, it's the same case. The last time I said that once I was present at the ARK Crisis Staff meeting, just once, and never again. Now, when we're talking about the Crisis Staff of Banja Luka, I was a member of the Banja Luka Crisis Staff. It was something that was upon orders and it did not last for very long, because the activity of the Municipal Assembly was discontinued. That's why. That's what I already said and that's what you can find in my testimony in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just by way of guidance, Mr. Radic, and following up on the Court's suggestion, I think the answer to that question would have been a simple yes, you were a member of the Banja Luka Municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. By ex officio, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like the witness to be shown an exhibit previously introduced in this case, and that's the December 19th, 1991 instructions, the Variant A and B document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, when this document is distributed, certainly there's a way of improving the logistics of documents, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you were shown this document in the course of your testimony in the Brdjanin case. And you are familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, this doesn't seem to be the one. We seem to have another piece of paper altogether, 22nd of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We received the paper of the ... Mr. Tieger, we received one document, 22nd of June, 1992; another document, the 23rd of June, 1992; and the second one without an original, just a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me see if I can proceed without taking the Court's time with the distribution of the Variant A and B document, Your Honour, based on some questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, first of all, do you recall the discussion concerning the instructions of December 19th, 1991, the so-called Variant A and B document? Do you recall a discussion during the course of your Brdjanin testimony?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: This isn't the document I'm holding.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. I understand that, sir. And it appears that you were handed the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have established -- so questions are put to you now without an underlying document.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: But what document are you referring to? I cannot really talk about it unless I know the title of this document of the 19th of December. First of all, I have to tell you that this document here was not signed by Mr. Brdjanin. That's what I've told you the last time as well. This one dated 22nd June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We will retrieve the document and have it available Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. after the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The relevant document has been found. I think that it's not an entirely new document for us. If it's put on the ELMO, I take it that -- and if perhaps the -- then the original. We have a problem anyhow in ... Mr. Tieger, do you have a copy of the English translation of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe we do, Your Honour. I think it can be found in binder 18, tab 35, but let's make sure we have it before ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's you who is going to examine the witness on it. I see we have here one with the number 100 on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With the very helpful intervention and assistance of the Registry, Your Honour, that document is at P65, tab 66, I'm advised. The witness will now have it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, having now had an opportunity - and please take your time if you need to peruse the document further - do you recall being presented with that document and discussing it briefly during the course of your testimony in the Brdjanin case?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: You seem to rely too much upon my memory. I would have to review the document. First I have to tell the Honourable Trial Chamber that nobody consulted me concerning my arrival here, neither on the Prosecution side or the Defence side, in order for me to review the documents in advance to be able to answer these questions. I think this would have been quite understandable. Regardless of the fact that I had a chance of looking at these documents in the Brdjanin case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, if you need more time to look at these documents, that time will be granted to you. Mr. Tieger, I do not know what other documents you would need at this moment or whether you'd prefer to have an early break and perhaps prepare a copy so that Mr. Radic could, during the break, have a further look at the document. I leave it up to you. But that would be one of the options.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In light of the witness's comments, I'm more than happy to take an early recess and permit the witness to take a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then preferably not the original that was -- that is in evidence, but if then perhaps copies could be made. And perhaps also copies in the -- of the original in B/C/S so that Mr. Krajisnik is able to follow the testimony of the witness. Mr. Radic, if you would perhaps give that document back to Madam Usher. A copy will be made. You will have an opportunity over the next break to read it again, consult it, and we'll have a break until 5 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed. But before doing so, Mr. Radic, did you have an opportunity to look at the 19th of December document again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic, did you attend the meeting in December 1991 regarding the introduction or distribution of this document?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I'm not certain, sir. If there are any records of the meeting, it would be useful to look at them. But I'm not really certain as to whether I was at this meeting on the 19th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the instruction arrive in all municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No. It's all right, Your Honour. I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, the question was: Did the instruction arrive in all municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: It probably did. I cannot really say for a fact that it had reached all the municipalities, but probably it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In accordance with the -- let me ask you to look -- first, you've had a chance to look these over, including the enumerated items. In accordance with the instructions, did the municipal SDS in Banja Luka establish a crisis staff, as indicated in the document, and specifically as indicated in item 3?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: The municipal SDS to form a crisis staff? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember how you received the document, or whether it was brought to you by any other member of the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Isn't there a prior question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There might be a prior question, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there is a prior question, because the question as put makes an obvious assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, I understand from your previous answer that you don't know whether you received the document, you don't recall specifically whether you received the document at the December 19th -- or the meeting on or about December 19th itself.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I don't recall being at this meeting at all, but having read this document here, I can see that this document was distributed to the municipal boards of the SDS and that's when this so-called partisan document was then produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I think the question Mr. Stewart had in mind is whether the witness received a copy of this document. Even if you did not attend the meeting, did you receive this document, a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please believe me when I say that I don't recall receiving it. But I know that there was a discussion on this document, because the presidents of the SDS municipal boards received them, as it says here. It says here that they were to receive them, and then act upon implementing them. Because this is a party document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, as we can see from the first page of the document, Mr. Radic, it bears the title of the -- and as you've just explained, it's a party document -- bearing the name of the SDS Main Board.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it correct that there are also local boards and municipal boards?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: There were municipal boards and there were branches in the local communes. Larger towns had municipal boards and had their local boards. Banja Luka, for instance, had 57 local boards because it had 57 local communes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did the local boards respond to the municipal boards and the municipal boards, in turn, respond to the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: The local boards received tasks from the municipal board and responded -- were answerable to the municipal board for what they had to do. And of course, the municipal boards must have been responsible to the Main Board, or, as we used to call it at one time, the central committee, the Main Board, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to the ARK Crisis Staff, of which you were a member, as you've noted. The ARK Crisis Staff covered a region of over 20 municipalities in the Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could have marked as the next exhibit in order a portion of the Official Gazette of May 5th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a decision we received already at an earlier stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I'm advised, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, I see two English documents and one B/C/S document, as I noted before. Is there one English too much or one B/C/S short? One of the 22nd of June, the other one the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would not be the document in question. The ERN range for the document that contains the portion to which I'll refer is 00882889 through 2938.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I'm sorry about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I should also note, I believe that's contained at P64A of the Treanor documents. I don't have the tab number here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Prosecution Exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll first check will it's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it's in the footnote material, and which is not transported every day into court. 28 binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, I'd like to turn your attention to the third page of that document, a decision on the formation of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And it's a decision adopted, as it indicates at the top of the document, on 5 May 1992. Do you have that document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to indicating the date of formation of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, it contains a list of the membership of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen that. It's on the other side. It's the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that membership includes General Talic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: From the army, soon to be the VRS?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was the head of the CSB; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the leading figure, leading representative of the MUP in that region?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the president of the ARK Crisis Staff was Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, among other things, Mr. Brdjanin was known for publicly disparaging or denigrating or publicly saying ugly things about Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he did not mince his words. He did talk a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you indicated in the course of your testimony in Brdjanin that you had ugly discussions with him about his extreme views against non-Serbs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: You should present me what I told you exactly about the ugly discussions, about his extreme views. I would kindly ask you to show me what it was that I said precisely, because I don't like hearing someone else telling me what I said. I'd like to see what I said. And yes, it is true that I did have such discussions with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the witness has answered the question, although not by reference to his earlier testimony, but by just answering your question. I don't know whether we are in any need to compare that, but since the Chamber has not read any Brdjanin transcripts, we have no view on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, before you testified in the Brdjanin case, you were interviewed on two occasions by representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One of which took place on 16 July 2001, and the other of which took place on 28 July 2002; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the course of the interview on 16 July 2001, did the following exchange take place: Well, I'm asking -- this is -- excuse me, Your Honour. This is on page 26, beginning at line 28. And this was Mr. Grady speaking, Mr. Radic: "Well, I'm asking you: Did you agree with his extreme views against non-Serbs?" And you responded: "I did have problems with him, but I resolved those directly. I would go to the TV. I'd go to the radio and confront him."

utterances.speaker: MR. GRADY
utterances.text: "What discussions did you have with Mr. Brdjanin about his extreme views?"

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: "Ugly ones."

utterances.speaker: MR. GRADY
utterances.text: "Okay. Tell me about those."

utterances.speaker: MR. RADIC
utterances.text: "You cannot not begrudge him saying things against mixed marriages. In any case, you have everything written down, everything he said, everything was taped and recorded, and as I said, I had huge problems trying to calm it down in Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Radic, does that refresh your recollection about having ugly discussions with Mr. Brdjanin about his extreme views against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, among the things Mr. Brdjanin said, did he say that only 2 per cent of Muslims would be allowed to remain in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: He didn't say that. Do you mean he told me or said it publicly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact -- were you aware of him saying that publicly?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I can't remember his having said it publicly and that it was recorded, about this 2 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember him saying that it was the obligation of Serbs over the next hundred years to wipe their feet from the foul non-Christians who have befouled this soil of ours?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: You know, things like that, there are a lot of things like that for me to be able to remember all the things that Mr. Brdjanin actually said. But quite obviously, if somebody says in the next hundred years, for example, over the next hundred years, then this was rhetoric, which was far from reasonable thinking. So I really can't remember his having used the term "over the next hundred years." But of course he did say lots of things. He said all sorts of things. But could you just tell me where he said "over the next hundred years." Is it recorded anywhere? Is he recorded as saying that, or did a witness say that he had said that? I'd like to see it in black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Radic, I'm not going to make a habit of engaging in a colloquy with you. My obligation is to ask questions and your responsibility is to answer them. However, in this particular case I am going to play a recording of just that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could have marked next V000-0577.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P357.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: CD will be 357 and the transcript will be 357A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Just one moment. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to put this particular recording in proper context, let me ask to have played first clip 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The sound is not what I expect it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, let me ask you first if you -- I see you're reading the transcript. Did you have a chance to look at the video as it was being played? I know you didn't hear anything, so you might not have drawn your attention to the video.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this was a rally held in the summer of 1994 about the question of ratifying a peace plan?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to hazard an attempt at clip 2 and hope that the video portion is operative for that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Distinguished Presidency of Republika Srpska, Gentlemen Deputies, People of Krajina, the Citizens of Banja Luka: We have gathered here today, seven days before we state our views at a referendum to hear the arguments and to remember the victims of this and everything that took place before, the war before, and many previous wars, in 1991, 1941, 1914, 198 -- 1875, et cetera. The victims of this particular war are our children. The victims of the previous war are our brothers, sisters, fathers, and mothers. The victims of the previous war are our fathers and grandfathers and the one before that are our grandfathers and great-grandfathers. All of them had just one goal: to live in large numbers and, graced by God, with their own people and nothing more, recognising that other peoples have the same right. "They say we do not want peace. How dare they say that, of a people whose anthem could consist of the following verses: Krajina is a bloody gown. Blood for lunch and blood for dinner. All of us eat bloody mouthfuls, never a peaceful day or rest. We dream of peace but not at any price, because no one ever gave us peace for free."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We move on to a later part of the rally, after you've spoken, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "There are no Islamic states on land that has been forever Serbian. There is no Muslim people. And the entire world knows this. There are only Serbian people in these parts. There are Serbs who are Orthodox, Serbs who are Catholics, and Serbs who are Muslim. Under 6: We must urgently determine Serbian territories and borders and present them to the Serb people for their acceptance, because there is no state without a set territory and demarcated borders. "Bosnia is an eternally Serbian land. Until the Turks came to these parts, Bosnia was ruled by Serbian kings. The Serbs have expelled the Turks, the Austrians, and Germans, and the Serbian partisans drove Hitler away from this territory. There is no Army of Republika Srpska, the Republika Krajina and Yugoslavia in these parts. Only the Serb army Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. can exist on this territory. If we want to have a Serbian state -- and we do want to, and must -- then every Serb's imperative, with or without a developed consciousness, must be unification or death, with faith in God and the fatherland."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, was that Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And he was a member of the ARK Crisis Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I think he was, yes. If it says so, yes, then he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn a portion of the remarks by Mr. Brdjanin on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Brothers and sisters, dear people of Krajina and all other patriots who had come to this meeting. We must not succumb to the greatest deceit that we are voting for war and peace. We are voting for the betrayal or rescue of Republika Srpska. Those leftist forces which are offering us coexistence again must know that it is the obligation of Serbs over the next hundred years to wipe their feet from the foul non-Christians who have befouled our country."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, I take it that refreshes your recollection about at least --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall later on in that same rally Mr. Krajisnik either responding to the comments of Mr. Kupresanin or expressing general approval at the remarks of the previous speakers?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I don't remember what it was that he said, because it's ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could play the next clip, please, clip 8.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Dear brothers and sisters, my dear people of the Krajina on both side of the Una River: Having heard these wonderful words by my predecessors, I feel great satisfaction at being at this gathering here today, satisfaction at seeing the fruits of our struggle for our homeland in actuality. I see the strength of our people. I see great patriotism and a great love of one's country. If to that we add the proven heroism of the Serbian people of Krajina, then, in Banja Luka and Krajina, we have here something that all the people of the world can be envious of."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could play clip 9, another portion of Mr. Krajisnik's remarks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] We wish to separate, because we cannot live together. I must add something to the discussion and to the address delivered by Mr. Kupresanin. If the Muslims do not wish to be Serbs, if they do not recognise it, then I believe them, because I can only feel sorry for anyone who does not want to be a Serb. Because they don't know how beautiful and glorious it is. That is why we need to separate. It would take a great war to force us to live together again. We don't need war to separate us. We are already separated. The war would be necessary for someone to assemble us together again in the same state. We want those rights, which were attained by all peoples in the former Yugoslavia. We want our own state."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic, you've mentioned and looked at some of the remarks by Mr. Brdjanin. Is it correct that he was put in his position by the leadership because he was very obedient?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what led the leadership to appoint him. Yes, it had to appoint him. It must have done. Now, what led them to put him in that position would be very difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, drawing your attention to the interview of July 16th, 2001, Mr. Radic. On that occasion you also discussed Mr. Brdjanin's position as president of the Crisis Staff. And if I can direct your attention and the Court's attention and counsel's attention to page 61 of the 16 July 2001 interview, beginning at line 10. You were asked by Ms. Korner: "Q. So you're saying his power derived from his position of deputy to the Assembly in Pale. You said: "A. Not only that he was a deputy. He was a minister at the same time."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "Q. But there were many other people equally deputies and equally ministers, Mr. Radic, who were not president of the Crisis Staff, were they? And you said: "A. That was the task he was given. He was very obedient. You couldn't order Erceg or Kupresanin. They're a little different." So it was your position on July 16th, 2001, Mr. Radic, that Mr. Brdjanin's obedience was an important factor in his selection as president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Most probably that was how it was. But there were other candidates. Of course, they selected him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as you said in July of 2001, because he was obedient and others could not be counted on for such obedience; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Once again, I repeat: I don't know what led the leadership to give the job to him and not to somebody else, somebody else in the Crisis Staff, presidents of the crisis staffs and so on. Because the deputies had to be in the Crisis Staff. But why was he selected as president? That's a question that I find difficult to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you did not find it so difficult in July of 2001 that you were --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness is a Prosecution witness. Once Mr. Tieger has had a couple of goes at asking him the question, he really ought, with respect, to move on then. This is not a Defence witness for Mr. Tieger to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, as the Court is aware -- first of all, let me say that I agree, as a general matter, that there are limits to any examination. As a general principle for this witness and similar witnesses, I think the Court is aware that the Prosecution rejects the formalistic distinction between a Prosecution witness and a Defence witness in a case where there is a witness who is so entrenched in the events and who -- well, in the case of an insider witness. And so I will -- I'm prepared to move on, but not because of the distinction that Mr. Stewart cites, and I think it's important that at this juncture we note that the Prosecution seeks appropriate latitude in addressing the issues raised by such witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I would have to reread your submission in this respect, but I remember that you explained the position of the OTP in this respect. But isn't it true that it also said that you would then apply for the Court's consent? It was not presented, as far as I remember, as something that would slowly slip in, but that it was something you considered that might be necessary. Or has the point come that you ask approval for this approach?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I think it wasn't -- I think the Prosecution indicated that it would proceed with the examination as appropriately as possible under the circumstances. I think we've done so. I'm not asking at this point for leave to go beyond the questions I've just asked. That may be necessary. But I think, as a general matter, we've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've clearly indicated that the situation is not the usual situation in respect of Prosecution witnesses. But I do understand that you now intend to proceed. So at this moment there's no urgent matter to be decided. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, is it also the case that you indicated during your previous testimony that Mr. Brdjanin had assisted individual Muslims and Croats in private, but that if he had publicly stated any of the things he had done for individual Muslims and Croats, he would probably have been removed from his position?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely it. And all those who helped had to do that without other people learning about it, just like at the present time. Those who were helped, who were assisted, don't dare say that they were assisted because of their own people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is it correct that public acknowledgment of such assistance by a Serb, in a leadership position like Mr. Brdjanin's, to non-Serbs would not only have been problematic for his position but, in fact, would have been dangerous?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Well, at all events they wouldn't praise him for doing it. Now, what would actually happen to someone like that, I can't say. But one thing is certain: He would be left without his job, without his post.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And have you stated in the past, and specifically in the Brdjanin case, that it would not have been healthy to behave in such a way?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: You mean to admit that he helped somebody, to acknowledge it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't have been healthy for that person, for the person in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the ARK Crisis Staff, did they -- did that Crisis Staff receive instructions from above, instructions from Pale?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to answer that question. Most probably there had to have been some instructions, because it's difficult to imagine that Brdjanin himself would have made any decisions on his own. Although there were such decisions taken by him personally, alone. But there were also some decisions that were signed but not signed in his own hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, when you testified previously in the Brdjanin case, Mr. Radic, do you recall being asked the following question and giving the following answer at page 22123, lines 3 through 8. Question by Ms. Korner: "Q. All right. The regional authorities got their instructions, is this right? And we will look what you said in interview in a moment. But is this right: They got their instructions from the authorities in Pale?" And your answer: "A. Surely they must have obeyed the instructions that were coming from the republican government. That's for sure." Was that a correct response, Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Correct. They had to receive instructions from someone about what they were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that someone was the republican authorities in Pale; correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Someone from a higher level, naturally. He could not have worked on his own initiative; he had to receive instructions about what he was supposed to do. But again, I have to say that some things were done without the knowledge of the people from the top. That's the transcript that you had occasion to see, the discussion between Mr. Karadzic and Brdjanin on the issue of the dismissal of managers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you're referring to the intercepted telephone conversation of November 1991? That's you nodding your head yes; is that right? Just an oral answer.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: That was the cause of the conflict, and the conflict was actually solved by Mr. Karadzic arriving in Banja Luka and telling them that they were not allowed to do this. Therefore, someone must have done this without his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the conversation in November 1991, just for clarification, is the one in which Dr. Karadzic and Dr. Vukic express concern about the fact that Mr. Brdjanin was talking about something that he should just be doing; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: There was another point that you missed here, which was the issue of forming one Krajina out of two Krajinas. This was another point there, but President Karadzic simply interrupted this. He actually prevented it, because it was an irrational move that could not meet with the approval, the understanding of the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think we've heard evidence regarding that issue before, Mr. Radic, but thank you. Now, in addition to receiving and obeying instructions coming from the republican government, did the Crisis Staff pass on instructions to the municipal level of authorities?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some of them implemented them; others didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the ARK Crisis Staff didn't create anything; they just forwarded what they received from a higher level.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I didn't say this. That's not what I said. They did -- it did produce something. I didn't say that it merely forwarded what had been sent to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't trying to paraphrase you on my own; I was actually quoting something you said on -- during the course of your Brdjanin testimony. And directing the Court and counsel's attention to page 22290, lines 18 through 24. It was again during the course of questioning by Ms. Korner. You were asked: "Q. Right. Now in respect of the decision that were -- we've seen from the regional Crisis Staff forwarded from -- to municipal, either SJBs or the municipal crisis staffs, were those instructions dreamed up by the region on its own or were they as a result of instructions coming from Pale?" And your answer was: "A. As I've already said, the crisis staffs did not create anything. They just forwarded what they received from a higher level."

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: For the most part, that was true. However, there were decisions, as I've said, that they had to withdraw later on, when pressed by those from above, like, for instance, the removals of managers. All those who were not members of the SDS, even if they are Serb, were supposed to be dismissed from their positions. However, Karadzic prevented this because this was not -- he put a stop to this because this was not an instruction that originated from Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And just to clarify: You're distinguishing efforts to remove or dismiss those who were non-SDS from efforts to dismiss non-Serbs or those considered disloyal to the Serbian Republic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: I'm not trying to make this effort. I'm simply saying that there were some decisions that had not been received from the republican level of Republika Srpska. And in the documents that you have, you will see that Bosniaks, many of them kept their managerial positions. This was something that was put to me later on, that was taken against me, was held against me, and this is something that you could also find in the intercepted conversations that you have of me being in the capacity of a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it correct that local, municipal Crisis Staff presidents regularly reported to the ARK Crisis Staff to give situation reports on events within their area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And with respect to some of the orders of the ARK that were communicated to the municipality crisis staffs, let me direct your attention and the Court's attention to a few documents. First of all, if we could have marked as the next exhibit, and I think this time it may be the one you already have, Your Honour, the order of 22 June 1992, which is 00916505 through 6506.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P358.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand you're somewhat familiar with this document, Mr. Radic, from your previous testimony, but let me direct your attention to a couple of --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- points quickly. First of all, the date of the decision is 22 June 1992. And it states under "Decision," "Only personnel of Serbian ethnicity may hold executive posts, posts are the information flow is possible and then /posts involving/ the protection of socially-owned property, that is, all posts of importance for the functioning of economic entities." And then it goes on. And I also want to direct your attention because we'll refer to it again to the number of the order shown right below the heading, which is 03-531/92.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Which number are you referring to? You mean the number on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct. The number indicated immediately below the heading, "Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Krajina Autonomous Region, Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. 531/92. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me next turn your attention to two other documents. First, our exhibit next in order, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you said when you mentioned the ERN numbers 505 up through 506, but I have a translation -- an original only of 505, it seems, and not of 506. Or do I have an incomplete copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to us that 506 is a different document altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a different document, but since Mr. Tieger now mentioned both pages... Mr. Tieger --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you look at my copy or if I could look at your copy, so that we -- I have -- first of all, I have got three pages, two in English and one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me try to address the problem in what I think is the simplest possible manner. If we just limit the exhibit to the single page, 6505.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, in that connection, if I could direct your attention to the next exhibit which we'll ask to have marked in order. That's a document emanating from the Petrovac Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff dated 25 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
